Rahul Vaid And Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 20
March, 2023

Author: Rajnish Bhatnagar

 Rahul Vaid And Ors.

entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Through: Mr. Rohit Tyagi, Mr. P
 Goswami, Mr. Shashank 
 and Mr. Sahil Giri, Ad
 versus
 State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr.

Through: Mr. Amit Ahlawat, App 
 with Insp. Surender.

Mr. Mohit Aggarwal and
 Advocates for R-2.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajnish Bhatnagar
 Order
Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No. 403/2018, under Sections 498A/406/354/377/34 IPC, registered at Police Station- Model Town, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.

4. The brief facts of the case are that petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 14.02.2015 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
Out of this wedlock, a girl child was born.
After sometime, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since July, 2017.
On 28.10.2018, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement/Compromise Deed dated 30.01.2023.
A copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13-B(2) of the Rahul Vaid And Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189605492/
1 HMA Act was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree of divorce dated 20.02.2023 passed by the learned Judge, Family Court, Rohini, Delhi.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A copy of the decree is already on record.
6. Petitioners and Respondent No. 2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by counsel for the parties.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.

She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force,
pressure or coercion.

As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 65,00,000/- (bearing no.
009765 dated 02.03.2023 drawn on HDFC Bank) has been handed over to respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed 7.
Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
10. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No. 403/2018,
under Sections 498A/406/354/377/34 IPC, registered at Police Station- Model Town, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom
shall stand quashed.

However, the rights of the child born from the wedlock of petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are left open to be adjudicated by him/her as and when he/she attains the majority as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ganesh V.
Sudhirkumar Shrivastava & Ors decided on 22.04.2019 in Civil Appeal Nos.4031-4032 of 2019.
8. Parties shall also remain bound by the settlement dated 30.01.2023.
9. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J MARCH 20, 2023 p
